levels.title_hi: जा रहा था · जा रही थी · जा रहे थे

items.pronunciation_notes: Four words and four beats, with the last two both carrying an h: ra-haa thaa.

learn.title_en: One word again, and it is the same word
learn.explanation_en: Swap हूँ for था and the continuous present becomes the continuous past. Nothing else moves — the stem was never going to, and the marker रहा tracks gender and number, neither of which changed. This is the second time the time axis has cost exactly one word, and it will be the last time you are surprised by it. मैं जा रहा था means I was going, which is a moment in the past rather than a habit in the past. The distinction you drilled at level ten holds across the whole grid, not just in the present column.

examples.note: A moment in the past, caught mid-action.
The level eight sentence with one word changed.
The stem पढ़ is unchanged, as stems always are.

common_error.why_en: There is only ever one auxiliary. The past replaces the present one rather than being added behind it.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · मैं · masculine · continuous past
practice.explanation_en: Bare stem, masculine marker रहा, and the past auxiliary था.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: मैं जा रहा हूँ. The second is the same cell one column to the left.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two long ii endings back to back, and both are held: ra-hii thii.

learn.title_en: Two words carrying the same information
learn.explanation_en: In the continuous past, both the marker and the auxiliary agree with gender and number — रही and थी are telling you the same thing twice. That redundancy is worth noticing rather than resenting, because it means the ending rhymes: रही थी, रहा था, रहे थे, रही थीं. If the two halves do not match each other, something is wrong, and you can hear it without working anything out. No other cell in the grid gives you that check for free.

examples.note: Feminine on both the marker and the auxiliary.

examples.english: the girl was going to school
examples.note: A feminine noun subject, and both words follow it.
The past of the question from level nine.

common_error.why_en: The marker and the auxiliary always match in this cell. Mixing them is audible even before you analyse it.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · वह (feminine) · continuous past
practice.explanation_en: Feminine singular on both words: रही and थी.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual past cell?
game.explanation_en: वह जाती थी. The second is past too, but perfective — she had gone.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three short e endings in a row, and the phrase runs fast because of it: ve jaa ra-he the.

learn.title_en: The cell is finished, and it took one level
learn.explanation_en: वे जा रहे थे completes the continuous past, and it should have felt like almost no work. That is because the grid is doing what it was built to do: you learnt the continuous marker at level eight and the past auxiliary at level six, and this cell is those two facts standing next to each other. Four cells of the nine are now yours, and you have learnt exactly two participle systems and two auxiliary sets to get them. The remaining cells are made of the same parts.

examples.note: Masculine plural on both the marker and the auxiliary.

examples.english: the boys were going to school
examples.note: A plural noun subject in the direct form, since nothing follows it.
रहना again, with its stem sitting against the marker.

common_error.why_en: Both agreeing words go plural. In this cell you can hear the mismatch, because रहा and थे do not rhyme.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · वे · masculine plural · continuous past
practice.question_read_as: jaanaa · ve · masculine plural · continuous past
practice.explanation_en: Masculine plural gives रहे and थे, and the two rhyme.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: वे जा रहे हैं — the same cell one column to the right of this item.

summary.recap_en: The continuous past is the continuous present with the auxiliary swapped. Both the marker and the auxiliary agree with gender and number here, so they rhyme — रहा था, रही थी, रहे थे — which gives you a free check on your own sentences.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the continuous past with the other persons, including the question that opens most accounts of what went wrong.

levels.title_hi: क्या कर रहे थे? · पढ़ रही थीं

items.pronunciation_notes: The phrase falls away at the end, with रहे थे both short and unstressed.

learn.explanation_en: This is the past of the question you learnt at level nine, and it does a specific job: it asks what someone was in the middle of. That is why it turns up whenever anyone is explaining themselves — you were interrupted, you missed a call, you were somewhere unexpected. Note that तुम keeps its plural agreement in the past exactly as it did in the present, so both रहे and थे are plural even for one listener.

examples.note: The casual register. आप for anyone you do not know.
The polite version, with identical agreement.
A different question word, and the verb is untouched.

common_error.why_en: तुम is grammatically plural whatever the past tense is doing, so both agreeing words stay plural.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: करना · तुम · continuous past
practice.explanation_en: Plural marker रहे with the plural past auxiliary थे.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual past cell?
game.explanation_en: तुम क्या करते थे — what did you use to do, as in for a living.

items.pronunciation_notes: खा is one long aspirated syllable with nothing after it: khaa.

learn.title_en: A transitive verb, still behaving normally
learn.explanation_en: खाना takes an object, and in the continuous past that changes nothing at all: हम is the plain subject, the marker agrees with it, and the auxiliary follows. This is the same point level nine made about the continuous present, and it is worth making twice, because the perfective is only two levels away and that is where transitive verbs stop behaving like this. Until then, treat every verb the same. The construction that separates them belongs to one aspect only.

examples.note: Plural marker and plural auxiliary, agreeing with हम.
खाना is the noun for food, and it sits in front of the verb as the object.
Another object, and the agreement still runs off हम.

common_error.why_en: The marker agrees with हम, not with anything the sentence is about. Mixing रही with थे breaks the rhyme.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: खाना · हम · masculine · continuous past
practice.explanation_en: Bare stem खा, plural marker रहे, plural auxiliary थे.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: हम खा रहे हैं — we are eating, right now.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three nasal endings in one sentence — याँ, and then थीं — and each is a hum rather than a full n.
items.gloss_en: feminine plural, where only the auxiliary shows the number

learn.title_en: रही does not go plural either
learn.explanation_en: The feminine marker is रही for one woman and for twenty, exactly as जाती was and बड़ी was before it. So in लड़कियाँ पढ़ रही थीं the plural is carried entirely by थीं. This is now the fourth construction in a row where a feminine marked ending refuses to distinguish number, and it is safe to treat as a law: nothing feminine in Hindi that ends in -ी ever has a separate plural. The number, when you need it, will be somewhere else in the sentence.

examples.note: Plural subject, singular-looking marker, plural auxiliary.
The singular, and रही is identical.
The same pair of forms with a pronoun subject.

common_error.why_en: The nasalised रहीं is not used here. The auxiliary थीं is already carrying the plural, and it carries it alone.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: पढ़ना · लड़कियाँ · continuous past
practice.explanation_en: रही for any feminine subject, and थीं for the plural.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual past cell?
game.explanation_en: लड़कियाँ पढ़ती थीं — they used to study, rather than were studying.

summary.recap_en: Four cells done and the pattern is now mechanical. तुम and आप stay plural in every tense, transitive verbs still behave like any other, and the feminine marker रही refuses to mark number just as every feminine -ी ending in this course has.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the two past cells side by side, and how to say something was not happening.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three breathy sounds in sequence — ढ़, ह, थ — and none should be dropped.

learn.title_en: वह पढ़ता था and वह पढ़ रहा था
learn.explanation_en: The same split as level ten, moved one column left. वह पढ़ता था says he used to study — a habit that held over some stretch of the past. वह पढ़ रहा था says he was studying at a particular moment, and says nothing about whether he did it often. English marks this too, with used to study against was studying, so the concept is familiar. What is worth practising is producing the right one under pressure, because both are past and both feel available.

examples.note: One moment, caught in progress.
A stretch of time, described as a routine.

examples.english: he used to study every day
examples.note: रोज़ still only fits the habitual, exactly as in the present.

common_error.why_en: रोज़ describes a repeated habit, and the continuous can only describe one stretch of time in progress.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: पढ़ना · वह · masculine · continuous past
practice.explanation_en: Bare stem, masculine marker रहा, past auxiliary था.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual past cell?
game.explanation_en: वह पढ़ता था. These four options are the four corners of two aspects across two times.

items.pronunciation_notes: Five words, and the two nasal hums bracket the phrase: maiṁ nahiiṁ at the front, nothing at the end.

learn.title_en: नहीं sits in front of the whole verb
learn.explanation_en: The rule from level seven applies unchanged: नहीं goes before the verb and nothing else moves. What is worth noting is that the verb here is three words long, and नहीं still goes in front of all three rather than inside them. Hindi treats जा रहा था as a single unit for this purpose, which is a useful way to think about it generally — the three words are one verb, and things that attach to verbs attach to the front of the whole group.

examples.note: नहीं in front of all three words of the verb.
The same placement, with feminine agreement behind it.
And again with a plural subject.

common_error.why_en: Splitting the stem from its marker breaks the verb apart. नहीं goes in front of the group, never inside it.

practice.question: मैं जा रहा था · negative
practice.explanation_en: The three words of the verb stay together and नहीं goes in front of them.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: मैं नहीं जा रहा हूँ. The last is habitual present with the auxiliary dropped after नहीं.

items.pronunciation_notes: सो is one syllable with a long open o and no consonant after it: so.
items.gloss_en: a verb whose continuous and perfective both matter

learn.title_en: सोना, and a look at what comes next
learn.explanation_en: सोना means to sleep, and its bare stem is सो. It is intransitive — you cannot sleep something — which matters because the next level opens the perfective, and every verb there will be intransitive for a reason. वह सो रहा था is he was sleeping, an action in progress. The perfective of the same verb, coming shortly, is वह सोया है, which means he has gone to sleep and is still asleep. Two aspects, one verb, and the difference is between the act and its result.

examples.note: The action, caught in progress.
A plural noun subject with plural agreement on both words.
अभी pins the sentence to this moment, so the continuous is the only option.

common_error.why_en: अभी means right now, and a word meaning right now cannot sit with the habitual.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: सोना · वह · masculine · continuous past
practice.explanation_en: Bare stem सो, masculine marker रहा, past auxiliary था.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: वह सो रहा है — he is sleeping now.

summary.recap_en: Four of the nine cells are finished. The habitual and continuous split the same way in the past as in the present, नहीं sits in front of the whole verb group however many words long it is, and the adverb test still decides the aspect when you are unsure.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the perfective, which describes an action as finished — and where the verbs are chosen very deliberately.

levels.title_hi: आया है · बैठा है · गया है

items.pronunciation_notes: Two long aa vowels with a y glide between them: aa-yaa.
items.gloss_en: the perfective participle, and how it is built

learn.title_en: A third base, and a short rule
learn.explanation_en: The perfective has its own participle, and it is the simplest of the three to build. Take the stem and add -आ; if the stem already ends in a vowel, a य appears to separate them. So बैठ becomes बैठा and आ becomes आया. वह आया है means he has come, and the है adds something specific: the action is finished and its result still holds. He came, and he is here. There is one more thing worth knowing now. The perfective can stand with no auxiliary at all — वह आया simply means he came — and that bare form is the ordinary way to narrate a past event, more common in speech than either वह आया है or वह आया था.

examples.note: Finished, and the result stands — he is here now.
No auxiliary at all. This is the everyday past and you will hear it constantly.
आना with a destination takes no postposition, exactly like जाना.

common_error.why_en: आता है is the habitual — he comes, as a routine. The perfective is about one completed arrival.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: आना · वह · masculine · perfective present
practice.explanation_en: Perfective participle आया with the present auxiliary है.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the continuous present cell?
game.explanation_en: वह आ रहा है — he is on his way. The second says he has already arrived.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ठ is retroflex and aspirated, so the tongue curls back and the breath follows: bai-ṭhaa.
items.gloss_en: a consonant-final stem, and the perfective as a state

learn.title_en: The perfective often describes a state, not an event
learn.explanation_en: बैठना means to sit down, and its stem बैठ ends in a consonant, so the participle is simply बैठा with no य needed. But the interesting part is the meaning. वह बैठा है is most naturally translated he is sitting — not he has sat. English uses a continuous there and Hindi uses a perfective, because the sitting-down is finished and what remains is the position. A whole family of verbs works this way: the perfective gives you the resulting state rather than the moment of change.

examples.note: The act of sitting down is complete; what you see is the result.
A place word slots in and the verb is untouched.
सोना behaves the same way — the falling asleep is done, the sleeping remains.

common_error.why_en: बैठ रहा है means he is in the act of lowering himself into a chair. For someone already seated, Hindi uses the perfective.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: बैठना · वह · masculine · perfective present
practice.explanation_en: The stem ends in a consonant, so the participle is बैठ plus -आ with no य.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual present cell?
game.explanation_en: वह बैठता है — he sits, as a habit. The first says he is currently seated.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two light syllables with a y between them, and neither is stressed: ga-yaa.
items.gloss_en: the one irregular perfective you already know

learn.title_en: जाना does not follow the rule
learn.explanation_en: By the rule from the last two items, जा should give जाया. It does not. The perfective of जाना is गया, which shares no letters with the stem at all — the verb simply borrows a different root for this one participle. This is the model verb of the module, so you met गया on the very first card, and it is worth knowing that its strangeness is real rather than something you misread. There are only a handful of verbs like this in Hindi and they are collected at the end of this module, so treat गया as the one exception you carry until then.

examples.note: Finished, and the result holds — he is not here.
The bare perfective again, which is the ordinary way to say it.
The destination takes no postposition, as always with जाना.

common_error.why_en: जाया is what the rule predicts and it is not a word. जाना takes गया, and it is the only common verb that does anything this drastic.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: जाना · वह · masculine · perfective present
practice.explanation_en: जाना is irregular in the perfective: the participle is गया, not जाया.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the perfective present cell?
game.explanation_en: वह गया है. The last one is perfective too, but past — he had gone.

summary.recap_en: The perfective participle is the stem plus -आ, with a य inserted after a vowel: बैठा, सोया, आया. जाना is irregular and gives गया. The auxiliary is optional here, and the bare perfective — वह आया, वह गया — is the ordinary way to narrate a past event.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the perfective across genders and numbers, and an honest word about why every verb in this block goes rather than does.

levels.title_en: Perfective present: agreement, and one missing piece

items.pronunciation_notes: Two vowels running together into one long glide, with no consonant between: aa-ii.

learn.title_en: The same three endings, a third time
learn.explanation_en: The perfective participle takes -आ, -ई and -ए, which are the same marked endings in a slightly different dress: आया, आई, आए. Compare them with जाता, जाती, जाते and with रहा, रही, रहे and the family resemblance is obvious. Three aspects, three participles, and all three agree with the subject the same way. Whatever else is complicated about Hindi verbs, the agreement is not — you have been doing the identical thing since बड़ा and बड़ी in Module 6.

examples.note: Feminine participle with the third person auxiliary.
A feminine noun subject, and the participle reads it.
The irregular verb takes the same endings: गया, गई, गए.

common_error.why_en: Not ungrammatical, but it means he. वह tells your listener nothing about gender, so the participle is doing all of that work.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: आना · वह (feminine) · perfective present
practice.explanation_en: Feminine perfective participle आई, and वह takes है.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the habitual present cell?
game.explanation_en: वह आती है — she comes, as a routine.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two vowels again, the second shorter: aa-e, and then the nasal auxiliary.
items.gloss_en: perfective plural, and why these verbs were chosen

learn.title_en: Why every verb in this block is one you cannot do to something
learn.explanation_en: आना, जाना, बैठना, सोना — all four are intransitive, meaning they take no object. That is not an accident of the examples, and you deserve to know why. In the perfective, and only in the perfective, Hindi treats transitive verbs completely differently: the subject takes a marker and the verb stops agreeing with it. So मैंने खाया, not मैं खाया. That construction is large enough to have its own module, and it arrives as Module 9. Until then, build perfectives only with verbs like these, and if you catch yourself wanting to say I ate or she read, wait — the sentence you would produce now would be wrong.

examples.note: Plural participle with the plural auxiliary.
A plural noun subject in its direct form.
The irregular verb, plural.

common_error.why_en: The participle goes plural along with the auxiliary. Fixing only one of the two is the recurring half-correction in this module.

practice.prompt_en: Conjugate the verb for this subject.
practice.question: आना · वे · masculine plural · perfective present
practice.question_read_as: aanaa · ve · masculine plural · perfective present
practice.explanation_en: Plural participle आए with the plural auxiliary हैं.

game.question_en: Which form belongs in the perfective present cell?
game.explanation_en: वे आए हैं. The third is the same aspect one column left — they had come.

items.pronunciation_notes: The participle and the auxiliary run together in speech, close to aayaa-huuṁ.
items.gloss_en: arrival and approach, one line apart

learn.title_en: One has arrived, the other is on the way
learn.explanation_en: This exchange turns on the difference between a finished arrival and one still in progress. आया हूँ says the coming is done and the speaker is here. आ रही है says the sister is somewhere between there and here. Same verb, two aspects, and the choice tells your listener whether to expect someone or start without them. Notice also that the answer in the second line is a complete sentence without any word for at — घर आया हूँ, with no postposition, because आना and जाना take their destination bare.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: नहीं, वह अभी आ रही है।
lines.read_as: nahiiṁ, vah abhii aa rahii hai.
lines.english: No, she is coming right now.

common_error.right: नहीं, वह अभी आ रही है।
common_error.why_en: The perfective would say she has already arrived, which contradicts the नहीं at the front of the sentence.

practice.question: मैं घर ___ हूँ।
practice.explanation_en: A single male speaker who has finished arriving, so the masculine perfective participle आया.

game.question_en: Listen to the third line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: बहन is feminine and singular, so the perfective participle is आई.

tts_strings: नहीं, वह अभी आ रही है।

summary.recap_en: The perfective participle takes -आ, -ई and -ए, the same marked endings as every other agreeing word in this course. Every verb in this block is intransitive on purpose: in the perfective, and nowhere else, transitive verbs take a construction that has its own module later on.
summary.next_up_en: Next: more perfective present, and then the perfective past — still with verbs you cannot do to anything.
